text:
sam: quick run of a focused fused-attn experiment — trying a "stitch+merge" epilogue path that fuses qkv pack -> bias/rope -> output epilogue. results below, surprised by tail latency spike on bursts.

anya: can you paste the exact command you used? sequence/batch shapes matter a lot here. :eyes:

sam: sure — command and raw numbers:
```
bench_fused --model=llama-13b --kernel=mergeflow-stitch --batch=8 --seq=2048 --iters=120
Throughput: 155 tok/s per GPU
p50: 12.2ms p95: 48.7ms p99: 112.4ms
CPU sys: 7% GPU util: 82%
```

kevin: thanks. p99 jump looks...odd for 8x2k. did you capture profiler (nvprof/nvtx) traces?

sam: attached flame snippet (hand-excerpt):
- fused_epilogue_kernel::compute 46%
- qkv_pack_kernel::load 18%
- kv_cache::page_fault_handler 7%
- batching::coalesce_wait 6%
flame link: https://artifacts/runs/2309876500/flame.svg

jia: kv_cache::page_fault_handler = red flag. Are you testing with paged-KV enabled? If pages are small and we do concurrent evict/commit that could block the epilogue and amplify tail latency.

priya: confirm — this run had paged-kv enabled (page_size=64KB) and warmup disabled, right?

sam: yes paged-kv=on, no warmup (to simulate cold bursts). observed that when 2+ requests hit same KV page we serialized in the VM layer.

kevin: possible fixes to try (quick list):
- increase page_size to 256KB to reduce cross-request contention
- add a non-blocking prefetch step in kernel selector when predicted seq_len>1024
- fallback policy: disable epilogue fusion if kv_page_conflict_rate > 0.1
- tweak batcher: cap coalesce window to 6ms under latency-budgeted routes

anya: I think epilogue fusion gives decent throughput but has more coupling to KV behavior. For short tails we should bias selector to non-fused kernels when page_conflicts or paged-kv enabled.

sam: agreed. rough micro-experiment plan:
1) run warmup preload of KV pages for hot routes (script below)
2) run page_size=256KB bench
3) enable prefetch in kernel-selector and measure p99 vs cost

prefetch script (one-liner):
```
for k in $(seq 0 7); do bench_prefetch --model=llama-13b --range=${k}: --pages=16; done
```

kevin: also pushing a small change to the selector: add sampling probe that measures "kv_page_conflict_rate" over 100ms sliding window. if >0.12, mark request as "kv-sensitive" and route to non-fused kernel. want me to land experimental flag?

sam: yes please. mark it behind flag runtime.kv_sensitive_routing=true and let perf-bot collect metrics.

perf-bot: artifact uploaded: https://artifacts/runs/2309876500/mergeflow-probes.tar.gz :white_check_mark: metrics stream id: run-2309876500-mergeflow

priya: I'll run the 256KB page experiment later today and post a short summary. if we still see p99 cliffs, we should consider adding lightweight per-request kv-tag so the batcher avoids mixing kv-sensitive and normal requests in a batch.

anya: good call. mixing latency-budgets in a batch is a known antipattern. also consider moving epilogue to a separate async lane where it can be preempted.

sam: thanks team — next steps: kevin enables selector flag in staging, priya runs page-size experiment, jia will check page fault traces to see if any HBM->DRAM moves coincide. i'll collect combined metrics and open a short RFC with rollback plan. :thumbsup:

kevin: ack, landing flag in 30m.

perf-bot: perf-dashboard: https://perfboard/internal/?run=run-2309876500-mergeflow

sam: closing loop once we have p99 under 70ms for the burst profile.
